long_description:
32nd New Zealand Microscopy Conference

Under the theme “Shaping the Future of Microscopy in Aotearoa New Zealand”, we warmly invite everyone involved in microscopy and microanalysis to attend our annual meeting.

This year, the conference will be held at the Pipitea Campus, Victoria University of Wellington, from 24-27 November 2026.

The conference aims to showcase advances in microscopy and microanalysis developed in New Zealand, covering a wide range of fields including biotechnology, materials science, environmental science, image analysis, artificial intelligence, data management, and homegrown technologies.

In addition, the programme will feature special interest workshops, including image analysis using QuPath, facility management, and a technology showcase.

Don’t miss out—register now!

long_description:
Let’s talk about grief.

This Is Grief: On the Road is a series of free community conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O’Connor for an honest, informal conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the tidy timelines, clichés and expectations we’re often given.

There is no right kind of grief, and no right way to show up.

You might be grieving someone you love. You might be supporting someone who is. You might work alongside grief in your community or simply want us to get better at talking about something that touches all of us.

You are welcome to come and listen. You don’t have to share your story, speak, or have the right words.

Friday 13 November 2026
12.30pm–2pm
Unity Books, Wellington
Free event

Kirsten is the author of The Year After Kahlia, STAY and Tiny Invitations, and founder of This Is Grief.

Come as you are.

Join us for a special free screening of I Carry It With Me Everywhere by Other Cinemas and The Neglected Miracle by Barry Barclay at Massey University, with kōrero from Arwa Aburawa, Turab Shah, and Hana Pera Aoake on Monday 9 November 6:15pm-9pm.

I Carry It With Me Everywhere was informed by interviews with first-generation migrants living in the UK. This short film weaves together the lives of multiple characters as they confront inherited ideas of belonging. The Neglected Miracle is a film that forms the culmination of five years of international research into the question of who owns our seeds. This involves interviews with corporations, scientists and everyday farmers in the developing world. This was shot over two years in eight different countries. 

We are very lucky to be joined by Turab Shah and Arwa Aburawa of Other Cinemas for a kōrero before the screening. They have come all the way from the UK, so don't miss this chance to hear about the film directly from its makers!

This screening is programmed in concert with the exhibition Unseen. Unheard. Unarchived. by Other Cinemas and Friends, curated by Hana Pera Aoake. The exhibition is on at Enjoy until 19 December.

Snacks and drinks provided!

The screening will be held at Massey Cinema, Old Dominion Museum Building (East entrance): 15 Buckle Street, Mount Cook, Wellington

(Block 10 Tokomaru, Pukeahu Mount Cook, Wellington)

This event is supported by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University. Enjoy's Public Engagement programme is made possible by the support of Wellington City Council.

The Neglected Miracle

Film by Barry Barclay. Narrated by Keri Kaa. A Pacific films production. Film courtesy of Aotearoa New Zealand Film Heritage Trust – Te Puna Ataata (ANZFHT) and Ngā Taonga (NT). Festivals: 1985 Wellington Film Festival (World Premiere), 1985 London Film Festival, 2009 NZ International Film Festival, 2013 imagineNATIVE (Toronto).

long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

long_description:
Restoring what was wounded. 

Recovering what was lost. 

Becoming who God created us to be.

 

Do you at times struggle to fully embrace your identity as a son or daughter of God? Do you feel like you know who you are in Christ, but struggle to walk in it completely?

Then this event is for you!

 

Join us for a powerful journey of healing, hope, restoration, and discovery of your identity as a son or daughter of God led by Sandra Sellmer-Kersten.

Through biblical teaching, prayer ministry, and compassionate support, you’ll be invited to encounter Jesus in the places where you’ve experienced pain and discover His invitation to healing and wholeness.

Whether you are personally seeking healing or want to gain some tools to help others walk in and embrace their identity in Christ, this event offers practical insights, spiritual encouragement, and opportunities for prayer and ministry.

 

Sessions include:

The Heart of a King: Restoring what has been wounded and broken.

The Remembering: Remembering who God says we are—and learning to live from that truth.

The Voices: Recovering what shame, fear, pain, and rejection have silenced.

The Forge: Reawakening the unique “song” God has sung over each of us from the beginning.

The Roots: Rediscovering what we were created for—and stepping into what God has entrusted to us with His power and authority. 

 

What to Expect:

Biblical teaching on trauma and healing

Opportunities to receive prayer

A safe, compassionate, and supportive environment

Encouragement, hope, and practical tools for restoration

Included in your ticket:

Morning and afternoon tea will be provided, but please bring your own lunch

A comprehensive manual, usually sold separately for $25

About Sandra:
Sandra Sellmer-Kersten is the founder of House of Nacham Ministries, New Zealand, which she leads alongside her husband, Peter. She previously served for nine years with Elijah House Ministries USA, where she worked as a prayer minister and teacher under the leadership of John and Paula Sandford. Since moving to New Zealand, Sandra began working alongside Elijah House New Zealand, where she facilitates schools, teaches lessons, and has served as a Small Group Leader for 14 years.

We’re bringing our Wellington community together for a relaxed evening of conversation and connection. This is less about formal presentations and more about meeting others in the HealthTech community, sharing experiences and learning from one another.

As part of this catchup, two of our members will share their career journeys, the different pathways that brought them into digital health and some of the lessons they have learned as women working in the industry. Come along for a drink, an open conversation and the opportunity to connect with people who understand the opportunities and challenges of working in HealthTech.

What to expect

5.00 pm-5.30 pm: Arrive, grab a wine and meet others from the Wellington HealthTech community

5.30 pm-6.30 pm: An informal member spotlight and conversation with Catherine Epps and Jennifer Anderson

Meet our speakers

Catherine Epps is Director, Medical Devices at Pharmac, a role she has held since 2023. The range of medical devices used across the public health system is vast, with technology playing an increasingly important role in how many of these devices function. Catherine has more than 20 years’ experience in senior leadership roles across public and private healthcare organisations in Aotearoa, including serving as Executive Director Allied Health, Scientific and Technical at Capital & Coast District Health Board. She later led a broad portfolio at WorkSafe focused on reducing work-related health harm, including carcinogens, mentally healthy work and musculoskeletal harm.

Originally trained as a speech-language therapist, Catherine is a Fellow of the Australasian College of Health Service Managers and a Chartered Director. She is currently Board Chair of Stroke Aotearoa New Zealand.

Jennifer Anderson works in biotech commercialisation, with a focus on technologies that improve human health. Her career spans New Zealand’s public and private sectors, including roles in technology transfer offices, early-stage investment firms and start-up companies. This experience has given her a practical understanding of what it takes to move science from the laboratory to the market, from intellectual property management and financing to building the right team. Jennifer is currently Business Development and Commercialisation Manager at the Malaghan Institute of Medical Research, where she helps identify promising innovations and supports their translation into the clinic.

Whether you’re well established in HealthTech, exploring a new direction or simply keen to meet others in the community, we’d love you to join us.

An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.

Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.

Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.

Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy

Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. long_description:
This workshop will demonstrate the very basics of Tukutuku where each participant will come away with a form of Tukutuku and knowledge to inspire their own mahi toi. 

All materials supplied. Prior to the workshop participants are encouraged to research Tukutuku patterns and become familiar with the meanings.

 

Artist biography.
Elena Rei
Ngāti Toarangatira, Ngāruahine, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Tama, Sāmoa 

Elena Rei’s creative practice sits within the realm of Te Whare Pora, weaving together customary and contemporary processes of raranga, whatu muka and tukutuku. Interlaced throughout her works are collective dreams, moments of remembering and profound experiences with the materials she uses. Much of Elena’s practice is intuitive, emulating the ways of her tūpuna and drawing from a visual language that has been woven through time. Her works reimage and make familiar our inherent connection to ngā atua wāhine, through themes of aroha, grief, whakapapa and reconnection. 

Elena studied design and textiles at Massey University, where she gained early insights into practices within Te Whare Pora. A formative experience during this time was learning tukutuku under the guidance of Kohai Grace during classes at Whitireia, an experience that continues to inform her practice today.

Moving between Afro, EDM, hip hop and analogue pop, Sam invites listeners into a story that is deeply his own while remaining relatable in its themes of belonging, change and connection.
A Painful Story is ultimately an exploration of what we carry with us, what we leave behind, and how we learn to make peace with the places and people that shape us.
This exclusive showing of A Painful Story, music, visuals and all is the first time the world gets to see the creativity, hard work and production mastery on display, in a one-off pre-release showing that you don't want to miss.

KIM CHURCHILL LIVE IN WELLINGTON!

One man. A guitar, harmonica, percussion and an extraordinary voice. A whole world of sound.

Australian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Kim Churchill returns to New Zealand for a very special evening of world-class live music at the beautiful Old St Paul's!

From the legendary stages of Glastonbury and the Montreal Jazz Festival to intimate venues around the world, Kim has built an international reputation for his captivating one-man-band performances, incredible guitar playing and heartfelt songwriting.

Blending folk, blues, roots and indie music, Kim creates a remarkable live experience. Intricate fingerpicking, rhythmic guitar percussion, harmonica, foot drums and soaring vocals somehow come together through just one performer.

His much-loved song Window to the Sky went platinum in Australia, and his music has reached millions of listeners around the world.

But it's on stage where Kim Churchill truly comes alive. His shows move from explosive, foot-stomping energy to beautifully intimate moments, with warmth, humour and stories from a lifetime spent travelling the world playing music.

Whether you're already a fan or discovering Kim for the first time, this is a concert not to be missed!

CONCERT DETAILS

📍 Old St Paul's, Wellington

📅 24 February 2027

🚪 Doors open 7:00pm

🎶 Concert starts 7:30pm

✨ Fully seated, intimate listening-room concert

ABOUT KIM CHURCHILL

Raised in the coastal town of Merimbula, Australia, Kim Churchill began his musical journey as a young busker before setting off around the world with a guitar, a surfboard and a remarkable talent for songwriting.

After winning the Byron Bay Bluesfest busking competition, Kim went on to perform at major international festivals, share stages with celebrated musicians and build a devoted global audience.

His distinctive one-man-band style is something that really needs to be seen to be believed. Combining technically brilliant acoustic guitar work with percussion, harmonica and a powerful, expressive voice, Kim creates a sound far bigger than one person should be capable of.

Yet beyond the extraordinary musicianship lies a gifted songwriter whose music reflects a lifelong love of travel, nature, connection and the freedom of the open road.

ABOUT THE VENUE

In the heart of Wellington, Old St Paul's is one of New Zealand's most breathtaking heritage venues, renowned for its magnificent timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and extraordinary atmosphere.

For one night, Nightingale Concerts brings its intimate listening-room experience to this iconic former church, offering audiences the chance to enjoy a remarkable Australian touring artist in one of Wellington's most beautiful and historic settings.

Expect an evening of exceptional music, heartfelt songs, extraordinary guitar playing and the kind of connection that makes live performance so special.

🎟️ TICKETS ARE ON SALE NOW!

From international festival stages to intimate concert halls around the world, Kim Churchill has captivated audiences with his extraordinary live performances.

Don't miss your chance to experience him up close in Wellington. Secure your tickets today!

long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

- Risk reduction strategies

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026
Matinee: 2:00 PM
Evening Performance: 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group Sunday retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

Join us for a special evening with Professor Sir Ashley Bloomfield as he returns to Tawa to share stories, reflections, and leadership lessons from his life and career.

From his connections with the Tawa community to leading New Zealand through the extraordinary uncertainty of the COVID-19 pandemic, Sir Ashley will offer a fascinating and personal look at the experiences that shaped him, the lessons he learned about leadership, trust and communication, and why strong communities matter when times get tough.

During the evening, Sir Ashley will share:

His personal connections with Tawa and what the community meant to him growing up, including his family's connections with Tawa Baptist and Tawa Anglican churches.

What it was really like leading through the COVID-19 pandemic - navigating enormous pressure and uncertainty, including more than 300 of those now-famous 1pm briefings.

Why trust and communication matter - particularly when the pressure is high and people are looking to you for clarity and direction.

What the pandemic taught us about community - and the importance of looking out for one another during difficult and uncertain times.

The experiences that shaped his approach to leadership - from training as a Territorial Infantry Officer to some memorable adventures hitchhiking around New Zealand.

Whether you're interested in leadership, community, New Zealand's recent history, or simply curious to hear the stories behind one of the country's most recognisable public figures, this promises to be a fascinating and memorable evening.

We’re bringing our Wellington community together for a relaxed evening of conversation and connection. This is less about formal presentations and more about meeting others in the HealthTech community, sharing experiences and learning from one another.

As part of this catchup, two of our members will share their career journeys, the different pathways that brought them into digital health and some of the lessons they have learned as women working in the industry. Come along for a drink, an open conversation and the opportunity to connect with people who understand the opportunities and challenges of working in HealthTech.

5.00 pm-5.30 pm: Arrive, grab a wine and meet others from the Wellington HealthTech community

5.30 pm-6.30 pm: An informal member spotlight and conversation with Catherine Epps and Jennifer Anderson

Meet our speakers

Catherine Epps is Director, Medical Devices at Pharmac, a role she has held since 2023. The range of medical devices used across the public health system is vast, with technology playing an increasingly important role in how many of these devices function. Catherine has more than 20 years’ experience in senior leadership roles across public and private healthcare organisations in Aotearoa, including serving as Executive Director Allied Health, Scientific and Technical at Capital & Coast District Health Board. She later led a broad portfolio at WorkSafe focused on reducing work-related health harm, including carcinogens, mentally healthy work and musculoskeletal harm.

Originally trained as a speech-language therapist, Catherine is a Fellow of the Australasian College of Health Service Managers and a Chartered Director. She is currently Board Chair of Stroke Aotearoa New Zealand.

Jennifer Anderson works in biotech commercialisation, with a focus on technologies that improve human health. Her career spans New Zealand’s public and private sectors, including roles in technology transfer offices, early-stage investment firms and start-up companies. This experience has given her a practical understanding of what it takes to move science from the laboratory to the market, from intellectual property management and financing to building the right team. Jennifer is currently Business Development and Commercialisation Manager at the Malaghan Institute of Medical Research, where she helps identify promising innovations and supports their translation into the clinic.

Whether you’re well established in HealthTech, exploring a new direction or simply keen to meet others in the community, we’d love you to join us.

In this one-time only public lecture at the National Library of New Zealand in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, David will share his thoughts on reading as a pathway to compassion, self-reflection and happiness—all with the characteristic David Hill warmth and wit.
With an introduction from journalist and award-winning author Claire Mabey, the Read NZ Te Pou Muramura Pānui is a public lecture held at the National Library of New Zealand followed by a printed edition available in a small booklet.
Current paid Read NZ members will receive a booklet free on the night, for others it’s available to purchase.
Entry is free Te Puna Mātaruanga o Aotearoa Auditorium at the National Library of New Zealand Bookings through Humanitix are essential Join us for celebratory drinks and nibbles in the foyer afterwards Printed copies of the Read NZ Te Pou Muramura David Hill Pānui will be provided to current individual members, with copies also available to purchase

id: "From Tawa to Oxford” An evening with Sir Ashley Bloomfield-1 Lyndhurst Road, Tawa, Wellington 5028, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: "From Tawa to Oxford” An evening with Sir Ashley Bloomfield
venue: 1 Lyndhurst Road, Tawa, Wellington 5028, New Zealand
long_description:
Leading self and others through unique and uncertain times

Join us for a special evening with Professor Sir Ashley Bloomfield as he returns to Tawa to share stories, reflections, and leadership lessons from his life and career.

From his connections with the Tawa community to leading New Zealand through the extraordinary uncertainty of the COVID-19 pandemic, Sir Ashley will offer a fascinating and personal look at the experiences that shaped him, the lessons he learned about leadership, trust and communication, and why strong communities matter when times get tough.

During the evening, Sir Ashley will share:

His personal connections with Tawa and what the community meant to him growing up, including his family's connections with Tawa Baptist and Tawa Anglican churches.

What it was really like leading through the COVID-19 pandemic - navigating enormous pressure and uncertainty, including more than 300 of those now-famous 1pm briefings.

Why trust and communication matter - particularly when the pressure is high and people are looking to you for clarity and direction.

What the pandemic taught us about community - and the importance of looking out for one another during difficult and uncertain times.

The experiences that shaped his approach to leadership - from training as a Territorial Infantry Officer to some memorable adventures hitchhiking around New Zealand.

Whether you're interested in leadership, community, New Zealand's recent history, or simply curious to hear the stories behind one of the country's most recognisable public figures, this promises to be a fascinating and memorable evening.

An Evening With a Purpose

From Tawa to Oxford is a fundraising event supporting the redevelopment of Tawa Anglican Church.

The redevelopment will create a welcoming facility designed to serve both the church and the wider community, with spaces for community groups, meetings, workshops, support services, events, and connection.

Proceeds from ticket sales will go towards the redevelopment project, so your ticket isn't just your entry to a special evening. It's also a contribution towards creating a community space that will serve Tawa for years to come.

Event Details

Wednesday, 4 November 2026

6:30pm

Emmaus Centre

Tickets: $50

Dessert & coffee provided

Come and hear the stories behind the public figure, discover the experiences that shaped his leadership, and enjoy a thought-provoking evening about navigating uncertainty, building trust, and the power of community.

Book your ticket and join us for From Tawa to Oxford: An Evening with Sir Ashley Bloomfield.

long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

PAYPA Hui & Awards Weekend 2026 – We’re heading to Circa Theatre!

The Annual PAYPA Hui & Awards Weekend is happening in Te Whanganui-a-Tara | Wellington. Join us as we connect with the performing arts sector, see incredible shows, and celebrate excellence in our community.

The 2026 PAYPA Hui is made possible with support from Creative New Zealand and Circa Theatre. Ngā mihi nui.

Click 'Join us' to RSVP to the PAYPA events below, including the workshops. Please note that tickets for After God will need to be booked via the Circa website link below.

FRIDAY 30TH OCTOBER

5pm - 7pm - Welcome Function

An informal chance to come together and connect over a pre-show drink.

7pm - 9pm - Performance - After God at Circa 1 - Tickets $30 (special PAYPA discount). Book your tickets via The Circa Theatre website and use code PAYPA26 at the end of the booking process

SATURDAY 31ST OCTOBER

9:30am-12pm - Workshop 1 at Circa 2 'So You Think You Know Me?' - A workshop on whakapapa, whakawhanaungatanga and the art of creating through connection with Regan Taylor

12pm - 1pm - Lunch

Join us for an evening of celebration and connection. Featuring performances by The KaRs & Musical Stars. A panel and community discussion about keeping connected, resilient, and what that looks like, as the sector moves forward into the future. And of course, we'll celebrate our wonderful nominees and winners of the PAYPA awards themselves!

9.45am -Walk and Talk with PAYPA - from Circa Theatre to Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library

Meet PAYPA Board members and enjoy the restored library building. A space for everyone to discover and connect.
